ryl lints general YAML, not the application that reads it, and its fixes never
change what a document means. Requests outside that line are declined, so check this page before filing
one.

## Rules for one YAML flavour

ryl has no built-in rules for GitHub Actions, Kubernetes, Ansible or any other
YAML dialect. Use the dialect's own linter alongside ryl:
[actionlint](https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint),
[kube-linter](https://github.com/stackrox/kube-linter) or
[ansible-lint](https://github.com/ansible/ansible-lint).

## Rules without evidence, or for contested style

A new rule needs more than one reputable source, such as the YAML 1.2.2 spec,
yaml.org, PyYAML's documentation or the yamllint maintainers, calling it best
practice. Blog posts alone don't count. Style with no broad consensus stays out,
for example:

- `null` versus `~`
- key-naming conventions
- flow versus block sequences
- exact blank-line counts

## Rules about application content

Rules check how a document is written and what YAML itself makes of it, such as
a truthy word, an implicit octal or a merge key overriding a value. They don't
check whether the values suit the application reading the file: sequence order,
allowed keys and value ranges belong to that tool. Mapping key order is form,
since YAML gives it no meaning, so `key-ordering` fits.

## Fixes that change meaning or reprint the document

`--fix` edits the document in place rather than reprinting it, and keeps its
resolved value, comments and anchors. That rules out:

- **Fixes that guess intent**, such as rewriting `no` to `false`: the author may
  have meant the string. One would only ever sit behind an explicit opt-in.
- **Whole-document reprinting**, the way Prettier formats YAML. Use a
  reprinting formatter if that is what you want; ryl won't become one.
  [`ryl format`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/formatter/) edits in place under the same guarantees.

## Not decided yet

ryl does no schema validation today; pair it with
[`yaml-language-server`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/editor-integration/) for that. Whether ryl should
validate against a user-supplied JSON Schema is an open question.

---

Source: https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/design/decisions/

# Design decisions

These are current, load-bearing choices from ryl's issues, pull requests, and repository history. Each Why records the published reason, or says "Not recorded" when no reason was found. [Scope](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/scope/) records declined requests, and the [migration catalog](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/getting-started/migrating-from-yamllint/#how-ryl-differs-from-yamllint) records compatibility differences.

## Priorities

When qualities conflict, work through these stages in order. An earlier stage wins only on a real conflict, and a later one still counts: meet it in a lesser form rather than dropping it. Where evidence is missing, keep the existing behaviour and ask.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  S[Scope and authority] --> C[Contracts] --> P[Predictable behaviour] --> R[Ranked preferences]
```

**Scope and authority.** The priorities decide choices within an authorised change; they never authorise one. A new default, flag, config key, output change or compatibility break needs the maintainer's agreement. [Scope](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/scope/), the decisions below, and the lint, test and coverage gates CI runs stand; changing a gate is the maintainer's call.

**Contracts.** These are never traded, against each other or anything else. If an edit cannot satisfy every contract, leave the input unchanged and report why.

- **Security.** A hostile payload never executes code, reads, copies, writes or appends outside the file being processed, writes through a symlink, or grows memory or time without bound, under the threat model in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/blob/main/SECURITY.md). Supply-chain checks are best effort. When containment and completeness conflict, analysis stops at its bound and reports fewer problems.
- **Never corrupt a document.** Resolved values, comments, anchors and untouched bytes are protected, and formatting and fixes are idempotent. Tests and debug builds enforce the guarantee, so release builds need not re-verify it.
- **Spec conformance.** ryl never writes invalid YAML or reports invalid input as valid, and the YAML 1.2.2 grammar and reference parser decide what YAML means. `format` and `--fix` may repair invalid input only where the output strict-parses and the relaxed input's events are preserved; a plausible guess at intent is not enough.
- **Supported platforms.** Behaviour holds on Linux, macOS and Windows; a platform-specific fast path is fine when every platform gives the same result.

**Predictable behaviour.** Configuration is explicit, local and fails loudly, except on the documented migration surfaces. Established ryl behaviour changes only through an authorised change with a deprecation path. For interface questions, follow the tool precedents below; for migration questions, the tool being migrated from.

**Ranked preferences.** Earlier wins:

1. **Runtime speed, where added complexity pays for itself.** A speed claim names its baseline, the workloads it affects, input sizes and run-to-run variance, measured on release builds. A change that adds code is accepted for speed only when its speedup on the affected workloads (old time ÷ new time) exceeds its code growth (new ÷ old lines in the modules it touches, counted by `tokei`; a new module counts as growth of the modules that call it), and no other workload regresses beyond variance; doubling a module's code needs more than double its speed. When judging a gain, weigh the default `check` and `format` paths on typical files above rare paths. A simplification must not slow any workload beyond variance, rare paths included. Design work may start from a cost model.
2. **Migration from other YAML tools.** Every competing linter and formatter has a clear migration path; a tool's behaviour decides only where its migrating users would break.
3. **Low peak memory.** Minimise it; when speed wins, report the memory cost.
4. **Simple, idiomatic code.** Less code, fewer branches, Rust best practice, and a repository layout that developers of ruff, rumdl, ty, biome or ripgrep recognise. Simplify wherever the items above are unchanged.
5. **Fast CI and local feedback.**

**Community.** These shape how work is done, not code trade-offs. Acknowledge every contribution and lower the bus factor: a safe contributor PR merges on its merits, and simplicity is restored in a follow-up rather than as a condition of merging. Docs and skills serve agents as users and contributors, within the always-on context budget.

## Precedent and trust

| Decision | Why | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **The YAML 1.2.2 grammar and reference parser decide parse disagreements.** The reference event stream takes priority even when other parsers agree against it. | The keep-scalar EOF case has the same reference value before and after formatting, while PyYAML and ruamel disagree; the spec's keep-empty production supports the reference reading. PyYAML and ruamel also accept YAML the spec rejects (yaml-test-suite 9C9N), so their agreement is no evidence of conformance. | [Spec and parser evidence](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/getting-started/migrating-from-yamllint/#block-scalar-at-eof), [maintainer decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/issues/694), [9C9N](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/issues/635) |
| **Eemeli's `yaml` cross-checks the reference parser.** PyYAML and ruamel are non-conformant and never outvote the reference, even 2–2. | The recorded yaml-test-suite comparison found `yaml` closer to the reference on valid and invalid cases; the keep-scalar case demonstrates the split. | [Parser comparison](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/getting-started/migrating-from-yamllint/#block-scalar-at-eof), [decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/701) |
| **ryl-yaml-parser supplies ryl's parse events.** Known divergences are recorded with examples in the migration catalog. | A single parser stack avoids conflicting event streams; published divergences make cases where ryl differs from other parsers reviewable. | [Parser stack](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/228), [divergence catalog](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/getting-started/migrating-from-yamllint/#how-ryl-differs-from-yamllint) |
| **ryl owns its parser as the `ryl-yaml-parser` workspace crate.** It is forked from granit-parser 2.0.0, never depends on ryl, and follows semantic versioning on its own API, independently of ryl's version; ryl is dual-licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0 to match. | Owning the parser lets ryl cut the formatter's memory and repeated scans without waiting on upstream; a separate crate keeps the parser reusable and movable to its own repository. | [Format performance](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/issues/787) |
| **Configuration is explicit, local and fails loudly.** Nothing runs from an unseen default, one nearest config governs each file, and anything ryl cannot apply is an error rather than a quiet warning. | Opening one file should show exactly what runs, and a typo or unsupported key must not look effective. | [Explicit and local](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/issues/291#issuecomment-4698540200), [unknown keys rejected](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/308) |
| **Ruff, rumdl, ty, and Biome are tool precedents.** Check their installed binaries where possible; a competing YAML tool decides only where migration compatibility would break. | ryl began from rumdl's example: a mostly single-developer Rust tool replacing Python Markdown linters showed the same could be done for YAML. rumdl itself draws on Astral's Rust tools (ruff, ty), so following their lead keeps ryl familiar to users of all three; competing YAML tools are migration paths, not models. | [Contributor policy](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/blob/main/AGENTS.md#coding-standards), [formatter re-review](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/issues/374) |

## Configuration

| Decision | Why | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Rules require explicit enablement.** A missing config or one enabling no rules exits 2, so an unconfigured run cannot silently apply a preset or lint nothing. | An unseen default preset would violate explicit rule selection; an empty selection would silently lint nothing. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/issues/248) |
| **TOML is the native configuration model.** Shared settings live at the top level, lint under `[lint]`, and formatter targets under `[format]`. Migration warns and rewrites the former flat lint keys. | Separate lint options from formatter targets while keeping common settings in one place; the shape matches Ruff's top-level, `[lint]` and `[format]` layout, so Ruff users meet no surprises. | [Epic](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/issues/374), [implementation](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/508) |
| **TOML configuration stays local.** One selected config governs a file; TOML has no `extends` inheritance or implicit preset selection. | One visible file should show every rule governing an input, without inheritance at a distance. | [Maintainer decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/issues/291), [Maintainer rationale](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/issues/291#issuecomment-4698540200) |
| **Legacy YAML configuration follows yamllint's surface.** Ryl-only settings and rules belong in TOML; YAML rejects unknown rule names and TOML-only keys rather than silently ignoring them. | YAML must remain a reliable yamllint migration surface; silently ignored keys make typos look effective. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/issues/191), [validation](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/441) |
| **Legacy YAML configuration is deprecated.** Conversion remains available while warnings name a usable migration command; the removal release is not yet set. | The TOML model can replace legacy execution only when existing YAML users have a working conversion path. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/issues/478), [warning](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/562) |
| **Deprecations need a usable target.** A warning starts only after its replacement exists, and stale configuration must never silently stop applying. | A warning before migration works would strand users, and silently dropping an old setting could change enforcement. | [Formatter epic](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/issues/374) |
| **Shared `indent-width` and `line-length` are defaults.** Formatter targets and lint defaults agree unless an explicit per-rule lint option overrides them; quote style remains formatter-owned. | Shared defaults keep ordinary lint and format settings aligned while explicit lint tolerances remain possible. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/issues/374), [implementation](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/521) |
| **Discovery prefers the selected project config.** Explicit CLI config wins first; project discovery precedes `YAMLLINT_CONFIG_FILE`, then native and yamllint-compatible user-global locations. | A project config should govern its files before a compatibility environment variable or user-global setting. | [Discovery](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/307) |
| **Project discovery walks ancestors and `.config/`.** A run from a subdirectory finds the governing project config, with native TOML candidates preferred in the documented order. | Subdirectory runs must find the project config; `.config/` supports an established repository layout. | [Ancestor fix](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/473), [`.config/` support](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/331) |
| **`YAMLLINT_CONFIG_FILE` accepts yamllint YAML only.** Native TOML uses `-c` or project discovery, keeping the compatibility variable's meaning unambiguous. | The yamllint-named variable should retain yamllint semantics, leaving native TOML to native discovery or `-c`. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/333) |
| **Ryl has a native user-global TOML path.** The native path takes precedence over the yamllint-compatible user-global YAML file when no project config governs the input. | Native users should not have to store ryl settings under a `yamllint/` directory. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/307) |
| **Invalid configuration fails visibly.** Unknown TOML keys or rule names are errors with exit 2, and the generated schema rejects them too. | An ignored key can make an invalid configuration appear to work, so loader and schema should fail loudly. | [Rule validation](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/249), [TOML validation](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/308) |
| **`ALL` and `--enable` are explicit shortcuts.** They select all rules or a command-line set without an implicit default preset. | Users need a concise explicit way to enable all rules or a CLI-selected set without restoring implicit defaults. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/490) |
| **Per-file and per-line ignores are TOML-backed suppression.** Path patterns and source-line regexes select where findings are ignored; the same suppression also governs safe fixes. | Mixed YAML repositories need targeted exceptions without maintaining separate configs or suppressing safe fixes inconsistently. | [Per-file](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/200), [per-line](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/288) |
| **Markdown linting is opt-in.** YAML and Markdown are separate source kinds; each embedded YAML region is checked independently. | Markdown contains YAML only in selected regions; opting in avoids scanning unrelated prose and file-shape rules. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/237) |
| **YAML config aliases have a bound.** The loader rejects expansion that would amplify a hostile config into an unbounded graph. | A short alias bomb could otherwise expand to billions of config nodes and exhaust memory. | [Hardening](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/249) |
| **Migration does not replace an active config.** A TOML config shadowing legacy YAML leaves that inactive YAML source untouched. | Rewriting shadowed YAML could produce a TOML file that changes which config is active. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/632) |
| **Migration flattens relative `extends`.** It checks the config directory before the current directory; a duplicate filename can therefore select different content from lint time. | Flattening inheritance preserves a standalone TOML result; the config directory gives relative paths a stable migration base. | [Review decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/307) |
| **User-global migration refuses relative `ignore-from-file`.** Its meaning depends on each linted file's directory, so one relocated TOML config cannot preserve it. | A relative ignore path depends on the linted file location, which a relocated user-global config cannot preserve. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/630), [guide](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/getting-started/migrating-from-yamllint/#what-is-preserved) |
| **Migration preserves disabled formatting intent.** A legacy rule that did not enforce a layout choice becomes an appropriate preserve target, avoiding a new formatting change. | Converting an unenforced legacy rule to an active formatter target would introduce an unwanted layout change. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/556) |
| **Top-level TOML file exclusion uses `exclude`.** `ignore` and `ignore-from-file` are deprecated there, while yamllint YAML and per-rule ignore spellings retain their meanings. | The new name distinguishes whole-file exclusion from per-rule ignores while migration warnings preserve old configs. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/608) |
| **Path matching follows the platform.** Configured paths compare ASCII case-insensitively on Windows and macOS and case-sensitively on Linux. | Matching normal platform path conventions avoids missed globs and config changes on Windows and macOS. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/653) |
| **Documentation examples use the real config loader.** CI validates examples through finalized configuration so misspelled rules and options fail. | The finalized loader is the source of truth, so CI should catch examples with unusable rule or option names. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/357) |

## Rules

| Decision | Why | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Rules report every problem they find, even where yamllint reports fewer.** | Fail loudly: a problem ryl detects is reported, never hidden. Complete diagnostics matter more than matching yamllint's output count. | Maintainer decision |
| **Built-in rules cover general YAML with evidence.** Application-specific schemas, unsubstantiated best practices, and contested style remain outside the rule set. | Rules should apply across YAML use cases and have evidence beyond a disputed style preference. | [Scope](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/scope/), [rules epic](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/issues/261) |
| **Ryl-only rules are TOML-only and opt-in.** Merge keys, tags, Unicode line breaks, and block-scalar chomping address portability or clarity without changing yamllint YAML config semantics. | These portability and clarity checks have no yamllint counterpart; TOML opt-in avoids changing YAML compatibility. | [Merge keys](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/276), [tags](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/272), [line breaks](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/270), [chomping](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/286) |
| **Inline disable directives are shared across rules.** `# ryl` is preferred; `# yamllint` remains accepted for migration. | One engine-level implementation avoids inconsistent rule behavior while retaining existing yamllint directives. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/243) |
| **Canonical duplicate-key checks are opt-in.** YAML 1.2 core-schema identity can flag keys yamllint treats as different spellings, so TOML enables that semantic mode explicitly. | Canonical identity can report duplicates that lexical yamllint checks miss, so users must choose the stricter mode. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/267) |
| **Tag allowlists use source spelling.** A user's non-core tag pattern matches what the author wrote, while unsafe-tag checks use the resolved identity. | Authors need to allowlist the tag spelling they wrote, while unsafe tags must not evade checks through alternate spelling. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/272) |
| **Quoted-string checks separate keys from values.** Mapping values are checked by default; rewriting keys requires `check-keys = true`. | The default follows yamllint, which checks values; users can opt into rewriting mapping keys. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/issues/290) |
| **A single-quote preference can permit necessary escapes.** The double-quote exception is an opt-in TOML setting because some strings need escapes a single quote cannot express. | Escapes available only in double quotes can make a strict single-quote preference impossible for some values. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/201) |
| **Truthy fixes do not guess intent.** A safe fix changes only case variants of the same YAML boolean, never `yes`, `no`, `on`, or `off`. | Re-casing an existing boolean preserves its value; rewriting YAML 1.1 words would assume the author’s intent. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/493) |
| **Key ordering remains a lint rule.** Its safe fix carries attached comments with a block mapping entry and leaves ambiguous cases unchanged. | Moving a key without its comments can attach commentary to the wrong entry; ambiguous mappings must remain unchanged. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/492) |
| **Key orders may depend on file and mapping.** TOML can place listed keys first and choose whether unlisted keys sort or stay in place. | Different files and mapping paths need different key orders, and unlisted keys need an explicit policy. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/494) |
| **Layout diagnostics stay in `ryl check`.** The formatter also enforces layout and warns if an enabled lint tolerance rejects its target. | Keeping layout findings in `check` follows Ruff and lets users lint without running the formatter. | [Maintainer re-review](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/issues/374), [Re-review](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/issues/374) |

## Formatter

| Decision | Why | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Formatting uses local span edits, never whole-document reprinting.** Resolved values, comments, anchors, and untouched bytes are protected; unsafe changes are reported and skipped. | Whole-document printers can change values, comments, anchors, and unrelated bytes; local edits support the preservation guarantee. | [Formatter epic](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/issues/374), [scope](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/scope/) |
| **Safe fixing promises soundness, not completeness.** A fix may leave a diagnostic behind; an ambiguous or unparsable region stays unchanged with a reason. | A guessed fix can change meaning or turn malformed input into misleading output; leaving a finding is safer. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/270) |
| **Meaning-changing repairs need explicit assumptions.** Default `--fix` preserves resolved values under a document's declared YAML version; an unsafe uplift would require opt-in configuration. | A safe fix must preserve the resolved value under the document’s declared version; other repairs depend on user assumptions. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/issues/365) |
| **`ryl format` has its own pass list.** Formatter targets do not inherit lint rule selection, fixability settings, or lint ignores. | Formatting should work independently of which lint rules or ignores a project enables. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/520) |
| **The formatter has built-in, overridable targets.** The linter remains explicit-rule-only; formatting works without a config and normalizes each option to a single target rather than a lint tolerance. | A formatter needs a definite target per option and should work before a user writes lint configuration. | [Epic](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/issues/374), [profile](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/issues/385) |
| **Document-start markers default to preserve.** Existing marker style remains unless the user requests a new target, replacing the initial add-`---` default. | Adding `---` to an existing file by default creates unnecessary changes; preserve matches formatter precedent. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/584) |
| **Unset indent width defaults to 2.** Configure `indent-width` to retain another width; lint `spaces` still defaults to `"consistent"`. | A fixed default removes seven candidate re-indents and follows other YAML formatters. | [Maintainer decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/issues/758) |
| **Line-ending auto uses the whole file.** The majority ending wins, a tie falls back to LF, and explicit LF remains the default. | The majority ending minimizes edits when auto is requested; LF remains the explicit default. | [Maintainer decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/issues/594), [Maintainer decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/issues/594#issuecomment-6091396339) |
| **Collection style has flat targets.** `[format]` can preserve, block-format, or flow-format sequences and mappings, converting only cases safe for their comments and values. | Collection presentation is layout owned by `format`; conversions must preserve values and comments. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/issues/446) |
| **Quoting preserves cross-version values.** Quotes remain when removing them would change resolution, including version-sensitive `y` and `n` spellings. | Removing a quote can change how YAML 1.1 or other common loaders resolve a scalar. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/560), [correction](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/604) |
| **Markdown boundaries can veto one region.** Formatting refuses an edit that would close a YAML fence or front matter early, while continuing with safe neighboring regions. | A changed delimiter could end a Markdown region early and turn YAML content into host text. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/633) |
| **Property tests gate formatter guarantees; the full corpus is optional.** Property tests check preservation and idempotence; a pinned real-repository corpus provides additional diagnostics. | Generated cases cover known invariants; the full corpus exposes patterns the generators missed but takes hours. | [Test policy](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/blob/main/AGENTS.md#automated-tests), [property suite](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/issues/379), [corpus](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/issues/386) |

## CLI and exit codes

| Decision | Why | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **`ryl check` names linting.** Bare `ryl <paths>` still lints with a deprecation warning, giving existing callers time to migrate. | An additive `check` command gave callers time to migrate before the formatter split changed the bare command. | [Command](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/370), [warning](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/461) |
| **`ryl format` writes by default.** `--check` and `--diff` inspect without writing and exit 1 when formatting is pending; stdin formatting writes to stdout. | Writing by default follows formatter command convention; inspection modes let CI detect pending changes safely. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/519) |
| **`check --diff` is a patch preview.** It leaves files alone, prints an applicable unified diff where possible, and exits 1 when a safe fix would change input. | Ruff-style patch previews support CI review and runners that apply a diff themselves. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/282) |
| **`-` reads stdin with an optional filename.** `--stdin-filename` supplies the diagnostic label, config discovery context, and path-filter context. | Editors and pipelines need to lint unsaved YAML; a filename restores file-based config and filtering context. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/issues/209) |
| **Markdown fixes splice back into the host.** Each embedded YAML region is fixed separately, retaining surrounding Markdown and rejecting boundary-breaking replacements. | Splicing isolated regions preserves the Markdown host and prevents file-shape fixes from escaping a fragment. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/241) |
| **Symlinks are readable inputs but not fix destinations.** Ryl lints a symlinked file and refuses to write a safe fix through its symlink. | Following a symlink during `--fix` could rewrite an unintended target in an untrusted tree. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/249) |
| **Input de-duplication is lexical.** Absolute paths are normalized without resolving symlinks, so distinct symlink paths remain distinct inputs. | Resolving symlinks would merge a symlink with its target and undermine symlink-aware fix handling. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/282), [Review rationale](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/282#issuecomment-4646614421) |
| **Output destinations are repeatable pairs.** CLI format and file targets override `[output]`, which overrides the console default; conflicting destinations fail with exit 2. | One run needs both console diagnostics and report files; paired targets make each destination explicit. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/303) |
| **GitLab fingerprints exclude location.** They hash path, rule, and message so a finding keeps its identity when line numbers move. | A location-free fingerprint remains stable when unrelated edits move a finding to another line. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/301) |
| **`ryl format` parses each file once.** Rule order guarantees value preservation and idempotence; release builds neither re-parse the output nor replan it, and debug builds check both. | A second parse and plan cost about 45% of format time from 64 KiB up; tests and corpus runs in debug still catch a rule that breaks the order. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/issues/834) |
| **Safe fixes converge in one invocation.** Ryl repeats the fix pipeline to a fixed point, with a bounded pass count and a visible non-convergence error. | Interacting fixes can expose later fixes, while a cap and visible error prevent an endless loop. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/467) |
| **Encoding does not make a pending change invisible.** BOM and UTF-16/32 inputs preserve their encoding through formatting; `--check` and `check --diff` still report changes when a byte patch cannot be shown. | An encoding that cannot carry an applicable text patch must still produce an accurate pending-change exit code. | [Format](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/617), [check](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/620) |
| **A write failure does not stop later files.** Formatting reports failed destinations, continues with the rest, and exits 2. | One unwritable file should not hide changes or failures in later inputs. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/714) |
| **Hook order gives formatting the final layout pass.** Run `check --fix` before `format` when both pre-commit hooks are enabled. | The formatter should make the final layout choice when both hooks rewrite files. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/705) |

## Parser authority

| Decision | Why | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Lint parses strictly; rewrites may repair indentation.** `check` and LSP diagnostics reject spec-invalid indentation; formatting and lint fixes require strictly valid output with the relaxed input's events preserved. | Strict diagnostics enforce YAML while guarded lenient parsing permits repairs such as yaml-test-suite `9C9N`. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/issues/635) |
| **One parser stack drives ryl.** ryl-yaml-parser supplies YAML events; a small local DOM supports configuration without maintaining a second parser implementation. | A single event parser avoids conflicting parse results and an unnecessary second parser dependency. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/228) |
| **YAML 1.2.2 grammar and the reference parser settle disagreements.** PyYAML and ruamel cannot outvote the reference event stream; eemeli's `yaml` is a cross-check. | The reference parser implements the spec event layer; the EOF keep-scalar case shows PyYAML and ruamel disagree with it even together. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/701), [EOF evidence](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/issues/694), [parser comparison](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/getting-started/migrating-from-yamllint/#block-scalar-at-eof) |
| **Resolution uses the YAML 1.2 core schema.** Plain `011` and `11` are the same integer key, replacing a proposed JSON-schema string reading. | One rule using JSON-schema identity would conflict with the core-schema resolver used elsewhere. | [Core decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/267), [wide integers](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/517), [Maintainer rationale](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/267) |
| **Each document's `%YAML` directive matters.** Unversioned input uses 1.2; explicit 1.1 keeps version-sensitive values, a higher minor warns, and a higher major errors. | Version-sensitive scalars can change meaning across YAML versions, so each document needs its own resolution policy. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/issues/351) |
| **Core tags resolve across spellings.** Verbatim and shorthand tags carry the same core-schema meaning in duplicate-key checks, quotes, and configuration. | Equivalent core tags must resolve alike regardless of handle or verbatim spelling. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/278) |
| **Bare CR is a YAML line break.** Rules and safe fixes share YAML 1.2's treatment instead of letting byte scanners disagree. | YAML 1.2 defines bare CR as a line break; separate byte scanners had disagreed with parser positions. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/287) |
| **Documented divergences stay deliberate.** Ryl checks comments after block-scalar headers even where yamllint does not, because the comment is still part of the author's YAML source. | The spec makes a block-scalar header comment part of the YAML source, even though yamllint misses it. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/496) |

## Packaging and release

| Decision | Why | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A public GitHub release is the final publication step.** Registry publishing must succeed first, replacing the earlier order that exposed the release before package feeds were ready. | A visible release before registry jobs finish can advertise binaries before package feeds are ready. | [Current decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/133), [replaced order](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/80) |
| **Release archives carry verifiable provenance.** Publish checksums and GitHub attestations with binaries so users can check an artifact against the release. | One checksum list and attestations let downstream installers verify the published binaries. | [Attestations](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/129), [checksums](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/325) |
| **npm uses platform packages.** The `@owenlamont/ryl` package resolves a platform-specific binary instead of downloading one at installation time. | Not recorded | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/168) |
| **Conda-forge builds from source.** Its feedstock follows staged-recipes and receives subsequent version bumps from the conda-forge bot. | Building from source on conda-forge covers platforms beyond ryl’s prebuilt binary matrix with little ongoing upkeep. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/issues/298) |
| **Winget follows a finalized release.** The release workflow submits x64 and arm64 archive URLs through `wingetcreate`. | Draft release assets are not publicly downloadable, but wingetcreate needs their URLs to calculate hashes. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/312) |
| **Winget fork sync failures fail the release job.** A dedicated fork-scoped token replaced the earlier warning-only treatment after a release submission failed. | A failed fork sync had blocked submission; the existing token lacked workflow permission without an overly broad grant. | [Current decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/469), [replaced warning](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/430) |
| **Downstream editor pins update after release finalization.** The release dispatch notifies `ryl-vscode` once the public release exists. | The editor bundles a pinned binary and had fallen behind because release completion sent it no signal. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/423) |
| **The changelog supplies release notes.** Published notes come from the matching version section rather than ad hoc text, including on draft reruns. | Versioned changelog sections provide one stable source for release text, including workflow reruns. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/677) |
| **Coverage is earned by named examples.** CI omits random property cases from coverage and replays saved seeds separately; local property runs retain their default counts. | Random examples can cover regions without a named regression test; saved seeds still replay separately. Skipping random cases also keeps CI runtime down on GitHub-hosted runners. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/668) |

## LSP and editor

| Decision | Why | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **`ryl server` reuses the check engine.** The default-on LSP feature is a thin protocol adapter; it complements the YAML schema server in an editor. | Reusing the check engine keeps editor and CLI results aligned while a schema server handles complementary features. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/316) |
| **A client receives one diagnostics channel.** Pull-capable clients get pull diagnostics; push is used only when the client lacks pull support, avoiding duplicates. | Clients supporting both channels otherwise display each finding twice. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/324) |
| **Unchanged workspace pulls wait for a change.** Result IDs report unchanged files, and a fully idle workspace request waits for an edit, watched-file event, or config change. | Immediate idle replies caused the client to rescan every two seconds; waiting avoids repeated full walks. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/424) |
| **Format Document uses `ryl format`.** Editor formatting follows the formatter even without enabled lint rules; Fix All stays a lint-fix action. | Editor formatting must use formatter settings even with no enabled lint rules, while Fix All applies lint fixes. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/583) |
| **Conflict warnings appear only for explicit changes.** Formatting and Fix All may warn about clashing formatter and lint settings; diagnostics and quick fixes remain quiet. | Warnings belong to an explicit rewrite request; diagnostics and lightbulb queries should stay quiet. | [Decision](https://github.com/owenlamont/ryl/pull/615) |

---

Source: https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/anchors/

# anchors

## What this rule does

Reports problems with YAML anchors and aliases &mdash; duplicated anchor
names, aliases that reference undeclared anchors, anchors that are declared
but never used, and (optionally) anchor/alias names that are ambiguous because
a `:` is welded to them. Projects can also forbid all anchors and aliases.

## Why this matters

- **Forward references fail at runtime.** An alias that points at an
  anchor declared later in the document is rejected by most YAML parsers.
- **Duplicates are silently ambiguous.** When two `&name` declarations
  share a name, downstream consumers may bind to either one depending on
  parser order.
- **Unused anchors clutter intent.** Removing dead anchors keeps the
  document's data-sharing structure explicit.
- **A `:` in a name means different things to different parsers.** YAML
  1.2.2 §6.9.2 lets an anchor/alias name contain any non-space character
  except the flow indicators `,[]{}`, so `:` is a *legal* name character.
  But parsers disagree where the name ends: ryl's parser, the YAML reference
  parser, and `ruamel.yaml` read `&foo:`/`*foo:` as the name `foo:` (colon
  included), while PyYAML/libyaml stop at the `:` (name `foo`, colon treated
  as a mapping separator). So a document of `a: &foo: 42` then `m:` / `- *foo:`
  resolves to `{a: 42, m: [42]}` under `ruamel.yaml` but raises a parse error
  under PyYAML — the same bytes, two different meanings. A single space
  disambiguates (`*foo : bar` is read the same way everywhere), so that is
  the form to use when an alias is genuinely a mapping key. Because ryl
  follows the spec here, the undeclared/duplicated/unused checks can differ
  from yamllint on colon-containing names; see
  [How ryl differs from yamllint](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/getting-started/migrating-from-yamllint/#how-ryl-differs-from-yamllint).

## Configuration

```toml
[lint.rules.anchors]
level = "error"
forbid-undeclared-aliases = true
forbid-duplicated-anchors = false
forbid-unused-anchors = false
forbid-ambiguous-anchor-alias-names = false   # ryl-only
forbid-anchors-and-aliases = false           # ryl-only
```

| Option | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `forbid-undeclared-aliases` | `true` | Report aliases (`*name`) whose anchor (`&name`) has not been declared earlier. |
| `forbid-duplicated-anchors` | `false` | Report when the same anchor name is declared more than once. |
| `forbid-unused-anchors` | `false` | Report anchors that are never referenced by an alias. |
| `forbid-anchors-and-aliases` | `false` | **ryl-only.** Report every anchor and alias, including valid declared-and-used pairs and aliases in merge keys (`<<: *name`). |
| `forbid-ambiguous-anchor-alias-names` | `false` | **ryl-only.** Report an anchor (`&name`) or alias (`*name`) whose name has a `:` welded to it &mdash; trailing (`&foo:`), internal (`&foo:bar`), or leading (`&:foo`) &mdash; the construct parsers disagree on. A space before the `:` (`*foo : bar`) is the unambiguous alias-key form and is never flagged. |

`forbid-ambiguous-anchor-alias-names` and `forbid-anchors-and-aliases` are
configurable only in TOML; YAML config rejects both options.

All `anchors` options are independent. No option suppresses or overrides another.
With `forbid-anchors-and-aliases` and `forbid-undeclared-aliases` enabled,
an undeclared `*missing` receives two diagnostics. The duplicated, unused and
ambiguous name checks also report their matching conditions when enabled.

## Examples

### :white_check_mark: Allowed

```yaml
---
- &anchor
  foo: bar
- *anchor
```

### :x: Reported (with `forbid-undeclared-aliases: true`)

```yaml
---
- &anchor
  foo: bar
- *unknown
```

### :x: Reported (with `forbid-anchors-and-aliases = true`)

```toml
[lint.rules.anchors]
forbid-anchors-and-aliases = true
```

Every `&` anchor and `*` alias below is reported, including the merge alias:

```yaml
defaults: &defaults
  retries: 3
job: *defaults
merged:
  <<: *defaults
```

### :white_check_mark: Allowed (with `forbid-anchors-and-aliases = true`)

Anchor-like text inside scalar values and comments is allowed:

```yaml
job:
  retries: 3
description: "Use &defaults and *defaults"
script: |
  echo '&defaults *defaults'
# &defaults and *defaults
```

### :x: Reported (with `forbid-duplicated-anchors: true`)

```yaml
---
- &anchor Foo Bar
- &anchor [item 1, item 2]
```

### :x: Reported (with `forbid-ambiguous-anchor-alias-names: true`)

```yaml
---
a: &foo: 42
m:
  - *foo:
```

## Automatic fixing

This rule does not auto-fix; anchor and alias graphs require human
judgement to rewrite safely.

## Related rules

- [`key-duplicates`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/key-duplicates/) &mdash; covers a related class of
  ambiguity in mappings.

---

Source: https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/block-scalar-chomping/

# block-scalar-chomping

## What this rule does

Requires every literal (`|`) or folded (`>`) block scalar to carry an explicit
**chomping indicator** &mdash; `-` (strip) or `+` (keep):

```yaml
script: |-
  echo "hello"
```

A bare `|`/`>`, or a header with only an indentation indicator such as `|2`, is
flagged because its chomping is still the implicit default.

## Why this matters

A block scalar header may end with a chomping indicator that fixes how the
scalar's *trailing* line breaks are handled (YAML 1.2.2
[§8.1.1.2](https://spec.yaml.io/main/spec/1.2.2/#8112-block-chomping-indicator)):

- `-` &mdash; **strip**: remove every trailing line break.
- `+` &mdash; **keep**: keep every trailing line break.
- *(none)* &mdash; **clip**: keep exactly one final line break. This is the
  default a bare `|`/`>` selects.

The clip default is implicit and easy to forget, so whether a block scalar ends
with a newline (or how many) silently depends on a detail that is not written
down. That trailing newline frequently matters &mdash; an embedded shell script,
a certificate, a key, or a templated config can behave differently with or
without it. Spelling the indicator out documents the author's intent at the point
it is decided.

An indentation indicator on its own (`|2`) is **not** a chomping indicator, so it
is still flagged: the chomping remains the implicit clip default.

Note that YAML has **no explicit clip indicator** &mdash; only `-` and `+` exist.
This rule therefore asks you to choose deliberately between strip and keep rather
than rely on the silent clip default; it cannot be satisfied by "making clip
explicit", because there is no such spelling.

Sources: YAML 1.2.2 §8.1.1.2 (block chomping indicator);
[yaml.info block-scalar chomp examples](https://www.yaml.info/learn/quote#chomp).

## Configuration

`block-scalar-chomping` is configured **only in TOML** &mdash;
`[lint.rules.block-scalar-chomping]` in
`.ryl.toml`/`ryl.toml` or `[tool.ryl.lint.rules.block-scalar-chomping]` in
`pyproject.toml`. YAML config (including `-d` data) rejects it.

```toml
[lint.rules.block-scalar-chomping]
level = "error"
```

The rule has no options: when enabled it requires an explicit `-`/`+` on every
literal/folded block scalar.

## Examples

### :x: Reported

```yaml
clip: |
  one line
folded: >
  some prose
indent_only: |2
  body
```

```text
1:7   error  missing explicit chomping indicator ("-" or "+")  (block-scalar-chomping)
3:9   error  missing explicit chomping indicator ("-" or "+")  (block-scalar-chomping)
5:14  error  missing explicit chomping indicator ("-" or "+")  (block-scalar-chomping)
```

### :white_check_mark: Allowed

```yaml
strip: |-
  no trailing newline
keep: >+
  every trailing newline kept
```

## Automatic fixing

This rule does not auto-fix. YAML has no explicit clip indicator, so a bare
`|`/`>` cannot be annotated without switching it to strip (`-`) or keep (`+`)
&mdash; which changes the scalar's trailing newlines and therefore its resolved
value. Choosing between strip and keep is the author's intent, so no single
rewrite is universally safe.

## Related rules

- [`indentation`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/indentation/) &mdash; its `check-multi-line-strings` option
  governs the *indentation* of block scalar content; this rule governs the
  *chomping indicator* in the header.

---

Source: https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/braces/

# braces

## What this rule does

Controls whether YAML flow mappings (`{...}`) are allowed and how much
whitespace they may contain.

## Why this matters

- **Stylistic consistency.** Mixing `{a: 1, b: 2}` and block mappings in
  the same file makes diffs noisier and intent harder to scan.
- **Tooling friendliness.** Some YAML consumers handle block style better
  than flow style; forbidding flow mappings can simplify downstream
  parsing.

## Configuration

```toml
[lint.rules.braces]
level = "error"
forbid = false
min-spaces-inside = 0
max-spaces-inside = 0
min-spaces-inside-empty = -1
max-spaces-inside-empty = -1
```

| Option | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `forbid` | `false` | `false`, `"non-empty"`, or `true`. Forbid flow mappings outright or only when non-empty. |
| `min-spaces-inside` | `0` | Minimum spaces between `{` and the first key (and between the last value and `}`). |
| `max-spaces-inside` | `0` | Maximum spaces at the same positions. |
| `min-spaces-inside-empty` | `-1` | Minimum spaces inside an empty `{}`. `-1` falls back to `min-spaces-inside`. |
| `max-spaces-inside-empty` | `-1` | Maximum spaces inside an empty `{}`. `-1` falls back to `max-spaces-inside`. |

## Examples

### :white_check_mark: Allowed (defaults)

```yaml
object: {key1: 4, key2: 8}
```

### :x: Reported (defaults)

```yaml
object: { key1: 4, key2: 8 }
```

### :x: Reported (with `forbid: non-empty`)

```yaml
object: {key1: 4, key2: 8}
```

## Automatic fixing

`ryl check --fix` adjusts whitespace inside braces to satisfy the configured
`min-spaces-inside` / `max-spaces-inside` bounds. The `forbid` constraint
is not auto-fixed because converting flow to block style requires
re-flowing the surrounding document. A minimum above its maximum cannot be
satisfied, so `--fix` leaves that spacing as it is.

`ryl format` writes one space inside non-empty braces when `[format] brace-spacing = true`, and none when it is `false` (the default). Empty braces stay `{}`. The formatter keeps flow style under the default `[format] mapping-style = "preserve"`. The rule conflicts with `forbid` when `mapping-style` is not `"preserve"`, or when its spacing bounds exclude the formatter's padding; see [Conflicting lint rules](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/formatter/#conflicting-lint-rules).

## Related rules

- [`brackets`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/brackets/) &mdash; the equivalent rule for flow
  sequences `[...]`.
- [`commas`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/commas/) &mdash; controls spacing between flow mapping
  entries.

---

Source: https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/brackets/

# brackets

## What this rule does

Controls whether YAML flow sequences (`[...]`) are allowed and how much
whitespace they may contain.

## Why this matters

- **Stylistic consistency.** Inline flow sequences read very differently
  from block sequences and projects often want one style throughout.
- **Predictable diffs.** Fixing the spacing rules avoids whitespace-only
  changes when editors normalise.

## Configuration

```toml
[lint.rules.brackets]
level = "error"
forbid = false
min-spaces-inside = 0
max-spaces-inside = 0
min-spaces-inside-empty = -1
max-spaces-inside-empty = -1
```

| Option | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `forbid` | `false` | `false`, `"non-empty"`, or `true`. Forbid flow sequences outright or only when non-empty. |
| `min-spaces-inside` | `0` | Minimum spaces between `[` and the first item (and between the last item and `]`). |
| `max-spaces-inside` | `0` | Maximum spaces at the same positions. |
| `min-spaces-inside-empty` | `-1` | Minimum spaces inside an empty `[]`. `-1` falls back to `min-spaces-inside`. |
| `max-spaces-inside-empty` | `-1` | Maximum spaces inside an empty `[]`. `-1` falls back to `max-spaces-inside`. |

## Examples

### :white_check_mark: Allowed (defaults)

```yaml
object: [1, 2, abc]
```

### :x: Reported (defaults)

```yaml
object: [ 1, 2, abc ]
```

### :x: Reported (with `forbid: true`)

```yaml
object: [1, 2, abc]
```

## Automatic fixing

`ryl check --fix` adjusts whitespace inside brackets to satisfy the configured
bounds. The `forbid` constraint is not auto-fixed because converting flow
sequences to block style requires re-flowing the document. A minimum above its
maximum cannot be satisfied, so `--fix` leaves that spacing as it is.

`ryl format` writes no spaces inside brackets, `[]` included, and keeps flow style under the default `[format] sequence-style = "preserve"`. It conflicts with `forbid` when `sequence-style` is not `"preserve"`, and with a `min-spaces-inside` or `min-spaces-inside-empty` above 0; see [Conflicting lint rules](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/formatter/#conflicting-lint-rules).

## Related rules

- [`braces`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/braces/) &mdash; the equivalent rule for flow mappings.
- [`commas`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/commas/) &mdash; controls spacing between flow sequence
  items.
- [`hyphens`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/hyphens/) &mdash; spacing rule for block sequences.

---

Source: https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/colons/

# colons

## What this rule does

Controls the number of spaces around mapping colons (`:`).

## Why this matters

- **Readability.** Consistent spacing makes columnar layouts easier to
  scan, especially in configuration files with many short keys.
- **Avoids ambiguity.** Stray spaces around the colon can hide subtle
  parsing bugs, particularly when keys contain values that look like
  flow-style content.

## Configuration

```toml
[lint.rules.colons]
level = "error"
max-spaces-before = 0
max-spaces-after = 1
```

| Option | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `max-spaces-before` | `0` | Maximum spaces between the key and the `:`. Use `-1` to disable. |
| `max-spaces-after` | `1` | Maximum spaces between the `:` and the value. Use `-1` to disable. |

## Examples

### :white_check_mark: Allowed (defaults)

```yaml
key: value
object:
  - a
  - b
```

### :x: Reported (defaults)

```yaml
key : value
key:   value
```

### :white_check_mark: Allowed (with `max-spaces-after: 2`)

```yaml
first:  1
second: 2
third:  3
```

### Alias, anchor and tag mapping keys

A YAML anchor/alias name or a tag may legally contain `:`, so `*anchor:` welds into an
alias to an anchor named `anchor:` (a parse error here, since no mapping colon remains),
and `&anchor: value` is the scalar `value` anchored `anchor:`. Using an alias as a
mapping key, or an empty key carrying only an anchor or tag, therefore *requires* one
separating space before the colon &mdash; `*anchor : value`, `&anchor : value`. That one
space is not reported; more than one is reported as usual.

```yaml
base: &a name
*a : value     # allowed: the one required separating space is not reported
```

```yaml
base: &a name
*a  : value    # reported (2:4): too many spaces before colon
```

## Automatic fixing

`ryl check --fix` trims the spaces before `:` and after `:` or `?` to the configured
maximum, never below the one space an alias, anchor or tag key needs before `:`, or the
one space YAML needs after `:` or `?`. A space after `:` that leads to `,`, `]` or `}`
is left to [`commas`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/commas/), [`braces`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/braces/) and [`brackets`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/brackets/).

`ryl format` writes no space before `:` (one for those keys) and exactly one after `:`
and `?`, turning a tab into a space. An explicit `?` or `:` that opens a block
collection continuing below has its spaces set that collection's indentation, so
`ryl check --fix` leaves it alone and `ryl format` re-indents the collection with it:

```yaml
? key
:   - a      # ryl format: `: - a`, with `- b` under `- a`
    - b
```

## Related rules

- [`commas`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/commas/) &mdash; the analogous rule for flow collection
  commas.
- [`hyphens`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/hyphens/) &mdash; spacing for block sequence hyphens.

---

Source: https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/commas/

# commas

## What this rule does

Controls the number of spaces before and after commas (`,`) in flow
mappings and flow sequences.

## Why this matters

- **Readability.** `[1, 2, 3]` is easier to scan than `[1,2 ,  3]`.
- **Consistent diffs.** Normalising comma spacing prevents whitespace-only
  diffs.

## Configuration

```toml
[lint.rules.commas]
level = "error"
max-spaces-before = 0
min-spaces-after = 1
max-spaces-after = 1
```

| Option | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `max-spaces-before` | `0` | Maximum spaces before the comma. Use `-1` to disable. |
| `min-spaces-after` | `1` | Minimum spaces after the comma. |
| `max-spaces-after` | `1` | Maximum spaces after the comma. Use `-1` to disable. |

## Examples

### :white_check_mark: Allowed (defaults)

```yaml
list: [10, 20, 30, {x: 1, y: 2}]
```

### :x: Reported (defaults)

```yaml
list: [10, 20 ,30,   {x: 1,   y: 2}]
```

### :wrench: After `ryl check --fix`

```yaml
list: [10, 20, 30, {x: 1, y: 2}]
```

## Automatic fixing

`ryl check --fix` normalises whitespace around commas to satisfy the configured
limits, leaving the spacing after a comma as it is when `min-spaces-after` exceeds
`max-spaces-after`. Before a closing bracket, the `brackets` or `braces` spacing wins;
where it contradicts these limits (yamllint's defaults on `[a,]`), the fix drops the
trailing comma. Disable with:

```toml
[lint]
fixable = ["ALL"]
unfixable = ["commas"]
```

`ryl format` writes no space before a comma and one after. It conflicts with a `min-spaces-after` above 1 or `max-spaces-after = 0`; see [Conflicting lint rules](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/formatter/#conflicting-lint-rules).

## Related rules

- [`braces`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/braces/) and [`brackets`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/brackets/) &mdash; spacing
  inside the flow delimiters themselves.
- [`colons`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/colons/) &mdash; the analogous rule for mapping colons.

---

Source: https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/comments-indentation/

# comments-indentation

## What this rule does

Requires that standalone comment lines line up with the surrounding
content. A comment may share the indentation of the line that follows it or, at a
dedent, retain the preceding block's indentation. At EOF, the preceding line applies.
A line-1 `#!` shebang or `#cloud-config` header is exempt, where yamllint
checks it: moving it would break the file.

## Why this matters

- **Visual grouping.** Comments that float at unrelated indent levels
  confuse readers about which block they describe.
- **Diff stability.** Aligning comments with their content makes it
  obvious when an edit moves or breaks the relationship.

## Configuration

```toml
[lint.rules.comments-indentation]
level = "error"
# Accept a comment aligned to any still-open enclosing block level (default false).
allow-any-open-indent = false
```

### `allow-any-open-indent`

This option is configurable in TOML only; YAML config rejects it. When `true`,
a standalone comment is also accepted if its indentation matches **any
currently-open enclosing block level**, not just the content that
follows it &mdash; useful for a comment that marks where a nested block ends. A
comment indented more deeply than every open level (or at a non-boundary indent) is
still reported. The default is `false`.

## Examples

### :white_check_mark: Allowed

```yaml
parent:
  # describes the child key
  child: value
```

### :x: Reported

```yaml
parent:
    # this comment is over-indented compared to `child`
  child: value
```

### :white_check_mark: Allowed with `allow-any-open-indent = true`

```yaml
config:
    entry:
        - things
    # aligned to the open `entry:` level — flagged by default, accepted with the option
options:
    - more stuff
```

### :wrench: After `ryl check --fix`

```yaml
parent:
  # this comment is over-indented compared to `child`
  child: value
```

## Automatic fixing

`ryl check --fix` reindents misaligned standalone comments to match the surrounding
content, leaving accepted comments unchanged. Disable with:

```toml
[lint]
fixable = ["ALL"]
unfixable = ["comments-indentation"]
```

`ryl format` applies the same fix, and no option of this rule conflicts with it.

## Related rules

- [`comments`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/comments/) &mdash; controls the formatting of comment
  text itself.
- [`indentation`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/indentation/) &mdash; the general indentation rule
  these comments are aligned against.

---

Source: https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/comments/

# comments

## What this rule does

Controls formatting of `#` comments &mdash; whether a space is required
after the `#`, and how far inline comments must sit from preceding
content.

## Why this matters

- **Legibility.** `#comment` and `# comment` read very differently;
  enforcing a space keeps comments visually distinct from directive-like
  prefixes.
- **Inline comments.** Pushing inline comments away from values prevents
  visual collisions when values change length; capping the gap keeps them
  next to the value they describe.

## Configuration

```toml
[lint.rules.comments]
level = "error"
require-starting-space = true
ignore-shebangs = true
min-spaces-from-content = 2
max-spaces-from-content = -1
```

| Option | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `require-starting-space` | `true` | Require at least one space between `#` and the comment text. |
| `ignore-shebangs` | `true` | Skip a line-1 `#!` shebang or `#cloud-config` header when `require-starting-space` is on. yamllint skips only the shebang. |
| `min-spaces-from-content` | `2` | Minimum spaces between code and an inline `#` comment. Use `-1` to disable. |
| `max-spaces-from-content` | `-1` | Maximum spaces between code and an inline `#` comment; `-1` (the default) disables it. Must be at least 1 and at least `min-spaces-from-content`. TOML only. |

Spaces and tabs each count as one. Setting `max-spaces-from-content` reports
deliberately column-aligned inline comments, and `--fix` collapses the alignment.

A comment after a block scalar header (`key: >- # note`) is checked like any other
inline comment, where yamllint skips it; see
[How ryl differs from yamllint](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/getting-started/migrating-from-yamllint/#comments-after-a-block-scalar-header).

## Examples

### :white_check_mark: Allowed (defaults)

```yaml
# a properly spaced comment
key: value  # inline comment with two spaces of padding
```

### :x: Reported (defaults)

```yaml
#missing space after the hash
key: value # only one space before inline comment
```

### :wrench: After `ryl check --fix`

```yaml
# missing space after the hash
key: value  # only one space before inline comment
```

### :x: Reported (`min-spaces-from-content = 2`, `max-spaces-from-content = 2`)

```yaml
first: value        # too far from its value
second: value # too close
```

### :wrench: After `ryl check --fix`

```yaml
first: value  # too far from its value
second: value  # too close
```

## Automatic fixing

`ryl check --fix` inserts the missing space after `#`, pads inline comments
to the configured `min-spaces-from-content`, and replaces a gap wider than
`max-spaces-from-content` with that many spaces. Disable with:

```toml
[lint]
fixable = ["ALL"]
unfixable = ["comments"]
```

`ryl format` follows `[format] comment-starting-space` and `comment-spacing`
(defaults `"add"` and 2). It conflicts when the configured comment gap falls outside
the lint spacing bounds; see
[Conflicting lint rules](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/formatter/#conflicting-lint-rules).

## Related rules

- [`comments-indentation`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/comments-indentation/) &mdash; controls the
  vertical alignment of standalone comments.

---

Source: https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/document-end/

# document-end

## What this rule does

Requires or forbids the YAML document end marker (`...`).

## Why this matters

- **Streaming consumers.** Producers that emit multiple YAML documents
  benefit from explicit end markers so consumers know each document is
  complete.
- **Single-document files.** Most single-document YAML files omit `...`;
  forbidding it removes a trailing footer that adds no information.

## Configuration

```toml
[lint.rules.document-end]
level = "error"
present = true
```

| Option | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `present` | `true` | When `true`, require a `...` marker at the end of every document. When `false`, forbid it. |

## Examples

### :white_check_mark: Allowed (with `present: true`)

```yaml
---
this: is the only document
...
```

### :x: Reported (with `present: true`)

```yaml
---
this: is the only document
```

### :white_check_mark: Allowed (with `present: false`)

```yaml
---
this: is the only document
```

### :wrench: After `ryl check --fix` (with `present: true`)

```yaml
---
this: is the only document
...
```

## Automatic fixing

`ryl check --fix` adds a `...` end marker to every document that lacks one
when `present: true`: before the `---` that opens the next document, and at
the end of the stream. The `present: false` case (removing existing `...`
markers) is never auto-fixed. A block scalar header or body at EOF gains the
newline and marker when the YAML 1.2 reference value is preserved. Spaces on a
final blank block-scalar line are removed only when they are indentation. A
root explicit-indent scalar with value-bearing final spaces keeps those spaces;
if its chomping indicator makes a marker unsafe, the final marker is left unfixed.

Disable with:

```toml
[lint]
fixable = ["ALL"]
unfixable = ["document-end"]
```

`ryl format` adds `...` the same way only when `[format] document-end` is `"add"`, and then conflicts with `present = false`; see [Conflicting lint rules](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/formatter/#conflicting-lint-rules).

## Related rules

- [`document-start`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/document-start/) &mdash; the matching rule for the
  `---` start marker.
- [`new-line-at-end-of-file`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/new-line-at-end-of-file/) &mdash; controls
  the final newline character.

---

Source: https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/document-start/

# document-start

## What this rule does

Requires or forbids the YAML document start marker (`---`).

## Why this matters

- **Multi-document streams.** Files containing more than one YAML
  document need `---` to separate them.
- **Explicit intent.** Requiring `---` even in single-document files
  makes the format unambiguous and clearly signals that the file is
  YAML rather than another similar markup.

## Configuration

```toml
[lint.rules.document-start]
level = "error"
present = true
```

| Option | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `present` | `true` | When `true`, require a `---` marker at the start of every document. When `false`, forbid it. |

## Examples

### :white_check_mark: Allowed (with `present: true`)

```yaml
---
title: example
```

### :x: Reported (with `present: true`)

```yaml
title: example
```

### :white_check_mark: Allowed (with `present: false`)

```yaml
title: example
```

### :wrench: After `ryl check --fix` (with `present: true`)

```yaml
---
title: example
```

## Automatic fixing

`ryl check --fix` adds a `---` start marker to every document that lacks one when
`present: true`: at the top of the file for the first document, and after the
`...` that ends the previous document for a later one. A UTF-8 BOM, leading the
file or a later document, stays before the `---`. A line-1 `#!` shebang or
cloud-init `#cloud-config` header stays first, with the `---` inserted after it,
since the interpreter or cloud-init reads it from byte 0.

The `present: false` case (removing existing `---` markers) is never auto-fixed
because removal can collide with multi-document boundaries.

Disable with:

```toml
[lint]
fixable = ["ALL"]
unfixable = ["document-start"]
```

`ryl format` adds `---` the same way only when `[format] document-start` is `"add"`, and then conflicts with `present = false`; see [Conflicting lint rules](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/formatter/#conflicting-lint-rules).

## Related rules

- [`document-end`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/document-end/) &mdash; the matching rule for the
  `...` end marker.

---

Source: https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/empty-lines/

# empty-lines

## What this rule does

Controls the number of consecutive empty lines allowed in the body of the
file, at the start of the file, and at the end of the file.

## Why this matters

- **Vertical density.** Too many blank lines fragment related content;
  too few make sections run together.
- **Trailing blanks.** Empty lines at the end of a file are usually
  unintentional and produce noisy diffs.

## Configuration

```toml
[lint.rules.empty-lines]
level = "error"
max = 2
max-start = 0
max-end = 0
```

| Option | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `max` | `2` | Maximum consecutive empty lines anywhere in the document. |
| `max-start` | `0` | Maximum empty lines allowed at the start of the file. |
| `max-end` | `0` | Maximum empty lines allowed at the end of the file. |

## Examples

### :white_check_mark: Allowed (defaults)

```yaml
---
a: 1

b: 2


c: 3
```

### :x: Reported (defaults)

```yaml
---
a: 1



b: 2
```

### :wrench: After `ryl check --fix` (defaults)

```yaml
---
a: 1


b: 2
```

## Automatic fixing

`ryl check --fix` trims runs of empty lines down to `max` (or `max-start`
and `max-end` for the leading and trailing run). The fix is **partial**
by design: blank lines that fall inside any multi-line scalar — literal
or folded block scalars (`|`/`>`), multi-line single- or double-quoted
scalars, or multi-line plain scalars — are left untouched, because
those blank lines contribute to the parsed value. Trailing blank lines in clip
(`|`/`>`) and strip (`|-`/`>-`) block scalars are trimmed because chomping
discards them. Keep (`|+`/`>+`) tails remain content and are preserved.
If such a tail exceeds `max`, the finding remains after both `ryl check --fix`
and `ryl format`; removing it would change the scalar value.

The protected line set is computed via the YAML parser, so the fix
bails (leaves the file untouched) when the input cannot be parsed.

Disable with:

```toml
[lint]
fixable = ["ALL"]
unfixable = ["empty-lines"]
```

`ryl format` caps internal empty-line runs at `[format] max-blank-lines` (default 2)
and removes empty lines at the start and end under the same limits. It conflicts
with a lint `max` below the configured cap; see
[Conflicting lint rules](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/formatter/#conflicting-lint-rules).

## Related rules

- [`new-line-at-end-of-file`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/new-line-at-end-of-file/) &mdash; controls
  the trailing newline character (distinct from "empty lines at
  end").
- [`trailing-spaces`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/trailing-spaces/) &mdash; reports whitespace on
  otherwise-empty lines.

---

Source: https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/empty-values/

# empty-values

## What this rule does

Reports keys whose value is missing (empty), separately for block
mappings, flow mappings, and block sequences.

## Why this matters

- **Accidental nulls.** A key without a value parses as `null`, which is
  often unintentional and can mask typos in the value.
- **Schema validation.** Some downstream consumers treat missing values
  differently from explicit `null`, leading to surprising bugs.

## Configuration

```toml
[lint.rules.empty-values]
level = "error"
forbid-in-block-mappings = true
forbid-in-flow-mappings = true
forbid-in-block-sequences = true
```

| Option | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `forbid-in-block-mappings` | `true` | Forbid empty values in block-style mappings. |
| `forbid-in-flow-mappings` | `true` | Forbid empty values in flow-style mappings. |
| `forbid-in-block-sequences` | `true` | Forbid empty list items in block-style sequences. |

## Examples

### :white_check_mark: Allowed

```yaml
---
some-key: value
explicit-null: null
```

### :x: Reported (with `forbid-in-block-mappings: true`)

```yaml
---
some-key:
other-key: value
```

### :x: Reported (with `forbid-in-flow-mappings: true`)

```yaml
---
inline: {first: 1, second: }
```

### :x: Reported (with `forbid-in-block-sequences: true`)

```yaml
---
items:
  -
  - value
```

## Automatic fixing

This rule does not auto-fix; supplying a value (including an explicit
`null`) is a content change that requires intent from the author.

## Related rules

- [`truthy`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/truthy/) &mdash; complementary rule for ambiguous bareword
  values.
- [`quoted-strings`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/quoted-strings/) &mdash; controls quoting of
  values, including the literal string `"null"`.

---

Source: https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/float-values/

# float-values

## What this rule does

Constrains how floating-point literals are written. Optionally rejects
implicit leading-decimal notation, scientific notation, and the special
values `.nan` and `.inf`.

## Why this matters

- **Parser compatibility.** Not every YAML consumer recognises `.nan` or
  `.inf`; forbidding them keeps documents portable.
- **Readability.** `.5` and `5e10` are valid YAML but can be misread.
  Requiring `0.5` and an explicit form makes intent obvious.

## Configuration

```toml
[lint.rules.float-values]
level = "error"
require-numeral-before-decimal = false
forbid-scientific-notation = false
forbid-nan = false
forbid-inf = false
```

| Option | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `require-numeral-before-decimal` | `false` | Require a digit before the decimal point (forbid `.5`, accept `0.5`). |
| `forbid-scientific-notation` | `false` | Forbid scientific notation like `1e6`. |
| `forbid-nan` | `false` | Forbid `.nan` literals. |
| `forbid-inf` | `false` | Forbid `.inf` and `-.inf` literals. |

## Examples

### :white_check_mark: Allowed (with `require-numeral-before-decimal: true`)

```yaml
factor: 0.5
ratio: 0.0
```

### :x: Reported (with `require-numeral-before-decimal: true`)

```yaml
factor: .5
```

### :x: Reported (with `forbid-nan: true` and `forbid-inf: true`)

```yaml
not-a-number: .nan
infinity: .inf
```

## Automatic fixing

This rule does not auto-fix; rewriting the literal requires care to
preserve the intended value.

## Related rules

- [`octal-values`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/octal-values/) &mdash; the analogous rule for
  integer literals in octal notation.
- [`quoted-strings`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/quoted-strings/) &mdash; useful when you want to
  pin a value to a string regardless of how it would otherwise parse.

---

Source: https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/hyphens/

# hyphens

## What this rule does

Controls the number of spaces between the hyphen (`-`) and the value in
block sequences.

## Why this matters

- **Alignment.** Consistent spacing keeps sequence items lined up under
  the same column, which matters for readability of long lists.
- **Diff stability.** Editors that "fix" hyphen spacing during a save
  produce noisy diffs when the rule is unset.

## Configuration

```toml
[lint.rules.hyphens]
level = "error"
max-spaces-after = 1
dash-on-own-line = false
```

| Option | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `max-spaces-after` | `1` | Maximum spaces between the `-` and the item value. |
| `dash-on-own-line` | `false` | Require the `-` on its own line when the entry is a block mapping (ryl-only; TOML config only). |

`dash-on-own-line` is configured in TOML only; YAML config rejects it.

## Examples

### :white_check_mark: Allowed (defaults)

```yaml
list:
  - first
  - second
```

### :x: Reported (defaults)

```yaml
list:
  -  first
  -   second
```

### :white_check_mark: Allowed (with `max-spaces-after: 3`)

```yaml
list:
  -   first
  -   second
```

### :x: Reported (with `dash-on-own-line: true`)

The mapping starts on the dash's line, so the `-` is not on its own line:

```yaml
items:
  - name: web
    port: 80
```

### :white_check_mark: Allowed (with `dash-on-own-line: true`)

The `-` stands alone and the mapping body is indented below it (a dash carrying
only an anchor/tag or a comment is also accepted, since the keys remain below):

```yaml
items:
  -
    name: web
    port: 80
```

## Automatic fixing

`ryl check --fix` trims the spaces after `-` to `max-spaces-after`, never below one.
`ryl format` leaves exactly one. `ryl check --fix` leaves a `-` alone when the block
mapping or sequence it opens continues on later lines, because the spaces set that
collection's indentation; `ryl format` closes the gap and re-indents the collection
with it:

```yaml
-   name: web    # ryl format: `- name: web`, with `port` under `name`
    port: 80
```

`ryl check --fix` does not fix `dash-on-own-line`. `ryl format` joins `-` and its block
mapping onto one line, or with `[format] dash-on-own-line = true` breaks the mapping
onto the line below; a dash line carrying an anchor, tag or comment is left as it is.

## Related rules

- [`indentation`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/indentation/) &mdash; controls how sequence items are
  indented relative to their parent key.
- [`brackets`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/brackets/) and [`commas`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/commas/) &mdash; the flow
  sequence equivalents.

---

Source: https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/indentation/

# indentation

## What this rule does

Enforces consistent indentation throughout the document. Specifically:

- The indent width used by block mappings and block sequences.
- Whether block sequence items are indented under their parent key or
  start at the same column.
- Optionally, the indentation of content inside multi-line block scalars.

## Why this matters

- **Mixed indents cause parse surprises.** YAML's whitespace sensitivity
  means inconsistent indents can change which key a value belongs to.
- **Cross-tool diffing.** Editors with different default tab widths can
  silently introduce mixed indentation; the rule catches drift early.
- **Convention.** Most projects settle on either 2- or 4-space indents;
  pinning the width prevents new files from drifting.

## Configuration

```toml
[lint.rules.indentation]
level = "error"
spaces = "consistent"
indent-sequences = true
check-multi-line-strings = false
```

| Option | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `spaces` | top-level `indent-width` if set, else `"consistent"` | An integer such as `2` for a fixed indent width, or `"consistent"` to lock the rest of the file to the first indent seen. |
| `indent-sequences` | `true` | `true`, `false`, `"whatever"`, or `"consistent"`. Whether block sequence items are indented under the parent key. |
| `check-multi-line-strings` | `false` | When `true`, apply indent checks inside block scalars and multi-line flow strings. |

## Examples

### :white_check_mark: Allowed (with `spaces: 2, indent-sequences: true`)

```yaml
parent:
  list:
    - item one
    - item two
```

### :x: Reported (with `spaces: 2, indent-sequences: true`)

```yaml
parent:
  list:
  - item one
  - item two
```

### :white_check_mark: Allowed (with `indent-sequences: false`)

```yaml
parent:
  list:
  - item one
  - item two
```

### :x: Reported (with `spaces: 2`)

```yaml
parent:
   over-indented: value
```

## Automatic fixing

`ryl check --fix` does not fix this rule; indentation changes can shift values into
different parents.

`ryl format` re-indents each block level to the top-level `indent-width`, or without it
to width 2 (see [Configuration](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/formatter/#configuration)),
with block sequences indented past their key unless `[format] indent-sequences = false`.
Block scalar bodies, continuation lines and comments move with the line they belong to,
